response.answer: To reach deployable accuracy, ASR requires thousands of samples per dialect, WER targets below 10%, and costs/time depend on dataset size and complexity. Generally, 100-500 hours of data per dialect is needed.

Accent and Dialect Adaptation in ASR: Training Custom Vosk Models to Improve Recognition for Non- Native English Speakers. This study explores the adaptation of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems to better recognize non-native English speakers through the training of custom Vosk models. As globalization increases the diversity of English speakers, conventional ASR technologies often struggle to accurately transcribe speech from individuals with varied accents and dialects. This research emphasizes the importance of accent and dialect adaptation to improve recognition accuracy, particularly for non-native speakers who may exhibit distinct phonetic characteristics influenced by their native languages. results.title: Evaluating an ASR in a Spoken Dialogue System | Skit Tech
results.content: The most popular metric that is used to evaluate the accuracy of an ASR model is WER or the word error rate. In this blog, we discuss metrics that can be used to evaluate an ASR, their flaws and suggestions for improvement in the context of a conversational agent. ## What is WER ? * Isolated word recognition (IWR-WER). WER is not input/output symmetric, as N is the total number of words in the actual transcripts. Improvements in WER’s over a test set is one of the standard ways of evaluating upgrades in an ASR. * WER is a purely 1 : 1 transcript based metric, and doesn’t take into account the rich output of ASR systems like alternatives or word lattices. Both communicate zero information, but the WER for ASR-1 is 2 and the WER for ASR-1 is 1. * **Character Error Rate (CER) :** Similar as WER with the smallest units as characters and not words. WER doesn’t look at the meaning of what has been transcribed despite the fact that is the semantics that are most relevant in an ASR that is a part of a spoken dialogue system. In this paper [9] they look at augmenting the WER metric for an ASR that is used for a Spoken Language Translation (SLT) task. The only change in this metric is that the substitution cost in WER is replaced by the cosine distance between the two words, so near identical words get assigned a very low cost. There are lots of different papers that augment the WER metric or introduce a new metric specific to a downstream task. results.title: Advanced Evaluation Metrics for ASR/TTS
results.content: While Word Error Rate (WER) for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Mean Opinion Score (MOS) for Text-to-Speech (TTS) provide essential high-level benchmarks, they often fall short in characterizing the performance details of sophisticated modern systems. * **Objective Intelligibility Metrics:** Metrics like STOI (Short-Time Objective Intelligibility) or ESTOI predict intelligibility scores based on signal properties, useful for evaluating TTS in noisy conditions. Kleijn, 2011 *IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing*, Vol. 19 (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)) DOI: 10.1109/TASL.2011.2114881 - Introduces the Short-Time Objective Intelligibility (STOI) measure, a widely used objective metric for speech intelligibility, relevant for TTS evaluation in noisy conditions.
